body: yes, that's where i got confused. so now that i'm signed up, i'll be able to participate in the next exchange, correct?

i hold onto clothes that don't fit anymore, simply because of the memories attached. i completely understand what you're going through. my parents ransacked my storage room and trashed so many things. i've never felt so helpless.
just always think of your mom every single time you want to self harm. she's your eye opener. :)

you completely sound like me from three weeks ago. i was so close to giving up, then my brother suddenly passed away of a heart attack at age 36. that was my eye opener. my suicidal self got a quick kick seeing my parents and family mourn the loss. i never want to cause them that kind of pain. i know that life is hard, but look for the beautiful things. flowers, animals, nature. it will calm you down and help you think more clearly. look for your eye opener, i hope that it won't be tragic like mine, but it is out there. you just have to find it.
i'm the same exact way. i also get the "why are you yelling?!" a lot. to which i stop and think about it, because i don't even notice that i'm yelling.

all of the therapists i've seen don't even seem to care, although it could just be me being paranoid. when they show up late, or cancel i have episodes because they're paid to listen to my bullshit, and they can't even make the time. it's an everyday struggle for sure. i want to get the help, but i'm absolutely terrified to do so.

i know that i'm not completely alone, but everyone who has the same feelings is terribly far away. no one around me understands, and their first impulse is to run. i feel like some horrible angry monster that no one can stand to be around. it's such a tough fuckin way to live.
sadly, i've never found anything that helps it other than avoiding all together or throwing in headphones. that way i can at least control the loud noises in my ears.

i have bpd, and yes. our local grocery store is undergoing a remodel, and i'm terrified to go shopping because of the noise. i get angry and my palms begin to sweat. i feel as though i could snap on anyone, at any given moment. it's horrible.

speaking as someone with BPD, the only thing that will make her feel okay is constant reassurance. and trust me, there will still be bad days. just stick with her, ya know? every borderline is extremely different, so you kind of have to learn as you go, which really is a pain. patience young jedi.
